copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Croatia v Ghana in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Saturday, and the model and the market disagree on the Croatia side by +19.0pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

The Elo prior reads Croatia 1860 vs Ghana 1620: 240 points in favour of Croatia, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Croatia to win at 67%, the draw at 16%, and Ghana to win at 17%. The home side reads 67% on this distribution — the model's central case for Croatia.

On the same three-way, Kalshi: Croatia to win at 48%, the draw at 26%, and Ghana to win at 20%. The Croatia side trades at 48% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +106. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 67%, +19.0pp wider.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Croatia the lower bound is 58%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +9.8pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. We're not arguing the market is broadly wrong; the closing line and the model are in approximate agreement across recent fixtures by Brier score. The claim is narrower: this side specifically reads mispriced.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff roughly 37 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Croatia a stronger prior than the Kalshi line implies.
The +19.0pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: On every meaningful read, Croatia look stronger here than Kalshi has them. Model 67% vs market 48% — a +19.0pp gap on the favourite side.
copy.title: Croatia v Ghana · the model leans Croatia
